the effects of glucocorticoids on cell proliferation in the developing palatal mesenchymal cells.
the mechanism by which glucocorticoids inhibit cell proliferation in palatal mesenchymal cells in vivo.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DEX-induced inhibition in arachidonic release is not a major contributor in either the cleft palate or the growth-inhibitory effects of DEX in palatal development.
DEX-induced celf palate formation and inhibition or palatal cell proliferation are not mediated by an inhibition of arachidonate metabolism.
DEX does not affect arachidonic metabolism in palatal mesenchymal cells and that DEX-induced clet palate and inhibition of palatogenesis is not mediated through an arachidonic pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inhibition of cell proliferation is a primary event in the mechanism of glucocorticoid action on the palate and is responsible for cleft palate formation.
DEX-induced c/fet palate is not caused by an inhibition of cell proliferation, and that the inhibition of cell proliferation is not mediated through inhibition of arachidonate metabolism.
DEX-induced inhibition in cell proliferation in the mouse palatal mesoderm is not mediated by the arachidonic cascade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DEX-induced growth inhibition in palatal mesenchymal cells is mediated by a mechanism independent of arachidic acid metabolism.
arachidonic metabolism is not the primary mechanism for DEX-induced growth arrest in palatal mesenchymal cells.
arachidonic acids are not responsible for cleft palate induction.
